C1.question: Highschool Grade Average
C1.commentary: More for prospective students what we were/are like. More significant negative correlations than positive ones here.

C2.question: Stream 4 Demographic
C2.commentary: Stream 4s tended to get more return offers, an easier 1B term, and were less likely to fail a midterm. However, they tended to have lower co-op wages compared to Stream 8s.

C3.question: Stream 8 Demographic
C3.commentary: Pretty much the opposite of Stream 4 since the math works out like that. Put more fields for positive correlation for variety.

C4.question: Computer Engineering Demographic
C4.commentary: They seem to take up the Full-stack and remote jobs. Did not show the negative correlations associated with EE roles, that will be shown in the EE demographic below. Overall not too many non-specific positive correlations.

C5.question: Electrical Engineering Demographic
C5.commentary: Pretty much the exact opposite so I went into more depth for the positive correlations.

C6.question: Sexual Partners
C6.commentary: Mostly what you would expect. Not many significant negative correlations (aside from being in ECE). The straight edge folks seem to not have any game, but also I do not condone unnecessary drug use (correlation does not imply causation).

C7.question: The Aphrodite Demographic
C7.commentary: People who are more likely to have used Aphrodite have -- used dating apps. Not much of a surprise here but some other interesting stats show up here too.

C8.question: The Goose Attack Victims
C8.commentary: The geese seem to hate people who grind Linkedin and LeetCode, but like richer old-money people. Not many significant negative correlations.

C9.question: If you got Policy 71'd
C9.commentary: Calling Harder was only the 4th most correlated statistic with getting P71'd. More educated parents tended to have kids who were not accused of P71 violations, so maybe they taught them better academic integrity or interest? Who knows? The main one here is that getting P71'd is typically observed less with people who don't have mental health struggles. Note: 2 metrics were removed from the top 4 because of their specificity to certain low population demographics

C10.question: All Nighters?
C10.commentary: People who pull all-nighters tend to sleep later on the regular. Not many strong negative correlations, but people who have OCD tended to just go to bed. Note: Grades were not part of this survey section, so we can't say if people who pull all-nighters may have gotten better grades.

C11.question: Mental Health Support Seekers
C11.commentary: Purely for insight on what kinds of people tend to seek mental health support and what they may do.

C12.question: Calling Douglas Wilhelm Harder
C12.commentary: Positive sample size is on the lower side, take with a grain of salt.

C13.question: Having Friends
C13.commentary: Breaking news: engineer learns that people with more friends were typically more social people. Lets just ignore the part where not doing drugs is negatively correlated.

C14.question: Time Spent on Social Media
C14.commentary: URA's spent less time on social media, likely because it's not really worth posting most of the time. Panic attacks was the most correlated, followed by specific low-demographic categories I omitted here to avoid identifying individuals.

C15.question: Going Out to Events
C15.commentary: For those guys who want to find a special someone, have you tried going outside? These are some of the strongest correlations in this entire section.

C16.question: Showering
C16.commentary: Surprisingly the males came out on top here when it comes to showering frequency.

C17.question: Exercising
C17.commentary: Exercising correlates positively with a lot of healthy and social activities, and negatively with mental health challenges. There were quite a few more mental health fields negatively correlated but were less significant so they were not shown here.

C18.question: Time Spent Sleeping
C18.commentary: Can't think of any generalizations here, just some interesting correlations.

C19.question: LeetCode Premium Subscribers
C19.commentary: Not many significant negative correlations, take them with a grain of salt.

C20.question: Linkedin Premium Subscribers
C20.commentary: There are people out there purchasing both LeetCode premium and Linkedin premium.

C21.question: Winning a Hackathon
C21.commentary: Please don't stop taking showers for the sake of possibly winning a hackathon. Just get more experience instead, seems to help more.

C22.question: Breaking Production
C22.commentary: Skipped a few single-person correlations, but people who break production tend to be the ones grinding.

C23.question: The Cali Or Bust Crowd
C23.commentary: Other than being in a casual relationship, the rest are fairly attainable for ECE. Most of you already have the non-existent mental health support -- just follow the rest of the tech-bro stereotype.

C24.question: Coop Satisfaction
C24.commentary: Co-op satisfaction seems to be tied to wages and return offers.

C25.question: Banned from WaterlooWorks
C25.commentary: The people who renege typically are chasing the bag. The good noodles seem to be the Stream 4s or the electrical engineers.

C26.question: Side Gigs During School
C26.commentary: No generalizations can be made here, most correlations were relatively weak aside from the obvious one.

C27.question: Side Gigs During Coop
C27.commentary: Something about these PMs doing side gigs during co-op. This isn't a low sample size either -- more than 25 PM co-ops were observed in this survey.

C28.question: Missed Interviews
C28.commentary: While some might conclude that missing interviews = better jobs, maybe consider that these people had lots of interviews so they had better jobs to choose from.

C29.question: Late for Interviews
C29.commentary: I highly doubt that being tardy for interviews causes you to have more job offers or higher co-op wages. It could be cope, but I wouldn't want to sabotage myself to find out.

C30.question: Average Co-op Wage/Salary
C30.commentary: About what you would expect. Omitted the per-term wages as those were on top with 0.48-0.73 correlation in descending order. Higher average wages typically mean your coops were better paid overall, but just because they are low doesn't mean you're stuck with a low paying full time job.

C31.question: Who Enjoyed FYDP
C31.commentary: People who enjoyed FYDP were happier people overall. No significant negative correlations, just going to spit out what the stats show.

C32.question: Failing a Term
C32.commentary: Less data here so conclusions here are less conclusive. Other than some of the expected ones, having more money and spending them on yourself seems to help and show that its tied to quality of life.

C33.question: Failing a Course
C33.commentary: With a difficult 3A term for most people, we don't see many generalizations here minus the being paid well. Remember that just because they are correlated, it doesn't imply causation.

C34.question: Failing a Final
C34.commentary: Failing a final may be more likely to fail the course, but not as likely to fail a term. Its not the end of the world if you fail, we all graduated here anyways.

C35.question: Failing a Midterm
C35.commentary: Similar to failing a final. Seems like the Stream 8s got it harder with the midterm in 2A.

C36.question: Cumulative Grade Point Average (cGPA)
C36.commentary: People with higher cGPAs tended to get higher-paying jobs and typically had an easier time with the harder terms (higher difficulty = harder, so negative correlation means they found it easier).

C37.question: Average Term Enjoyment
C37.commentary: Omitted the per term entries, but order was 4B > 4A > 1A > 3B > 2A > 1B > 3A > 2B for term enjoyment.

C38.question: Who has Committed Tax Fraud?
C38.commentary: Not a large 'yes' population so the stats here can be inaccurate. Omitted quite a few single-person correlations but left some funny/interesting/legitimately correlated columns.

C39.question: Gauges for Higher Full-Time Salaries
C39.commentary: Typical grindset correlations, omitted some stats with coop information prior to the 5th term or roles/locations with few data points.

C40.question: Full Time Job Satisfaction
C40.commentary: Not many negative correlations that are after coop 4. Negative correlation on term difficulty means that they found the term easier.

C41.question: Number of Job Offers
C41.commentary: Strangely enough people with more job offers had less diverse investments. We also see people with good last coops have fewer offers as they likely settled on a return offer.

C42.question: Diverse Investments
C42.commentary: This only counts the number of types of investments, not the cumulative amounts in investments.

C43.question: Graduating In Debt
C43.commentary: Apparently getting a coop job through recruitment events is tied to student loan debt? Or maybe the parents are paying off tuition and employers for jobs? We will never know...
